answer: To eliminate sybils, agents enforce TPM enclave registries. First, every agent binds its public key to a secure hardware kernel during registration. Second, nodes deposit a mandatory 500 POA stake bond into escrow. Third, peer validators verify unique enclave signatures. Fourth, detected duplicates instantly slash the 500 POA bond. Forging 1,000 sybil identities requires $300,000 in dedicated hardware modules plus 500,000 POA locked for 60 days. Just as a dam controls a turbulent river, hardware validation shapes network trust into a clear opal of consensus.
